title: Decision Tree
description: Non-parametric supervised learning method for classification and regression.
name: Decision Tree
summary: Decision Trees split data recursively based on feature values, optimizing for impurity reduction (like Gini or Entropy for classification, or MSE for regression) to create a flowchart-like structure.
use_when: Requiring a highly explainable, non-linear classifier that natively handles mixed data types.
avoid_when: Generalization on unseen data is critical without assembling trees into random forests.
pros: Extremely easy to visualize and explain to non-technical stakeholders.
Natively handles both categorical and numerical features without encoding.
Requires minimal data preprocessing, such as scaling or centering.
cons: High tendency to overfit training data if left unpruned.
Very sensitive to small variations in the training dataset.
Unstable decision boundaries compared to linear models.

key_hyperparams.name: max_depth
key_hyperparams.note: The maximum depth of the tree. Limits overfitting if set to a small integer.

quick_start:
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier
import numpy as np

X = np.array([[0, 0], [1, 1]])
y = np.array([0, 1])
clf = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=3).fit(X, y)
preds = clf.predict([[0.8, 0.8]])
